summary.headline: Motherson Sumi Wiring Q1 FY27 revenue grew 37% YoY, but copper and minimum-wage costs hit profitability; ~INR600 crore employee cost line flagged.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as resilient, with revenue growth outpacing the industry despite cost headwinds from elevated copper prices and sharply higher manpower costs after government-mandated minimum wage increases. Of the 37% revenue growth, management attributed 7 percentage points to copper pass-through and the rest to volume, content, premiumisation and new model launches. Greenfield plants held their prior-quarter run-rate of about INR450 crore and remained at break-even, with no meaningful profit contribution yet. Copper pass-through is still on a 3 to 6 month lag, with the quarter-on-quarter lag delta reduced to about 7% from 17% previously. EVs were 8.5% of revenue.

segments.name: Greenfield plants (three new plants)
segments.commentary: Revenue run-rate held at ~INR450 crore, same as prior quarter, with break-even maintained; some plants still ramping and expected to contribute to profit in one or two quarters. Management declined to disclose plant-level EBITDA or revenue split.

segments.name: EV vs ICE business
segments.commentary: EV-related business was 8.5% of Q1 revenue. Management said this is EV versus ICE business, not high-voltage alone, and gave no further breakdown.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance given. Management targets return on capital employed above 40%.
Staff cost trajectory depends on other state governments' minimum wage actions; nothing concluded yet, and the current mandated increase is fully reflected in Q1 results.

Customer recovery of wage increases is under 'constructive discussion' with no timeline. Management said most customers are on a 3-month pass-through cycle, with some pending price hikes from March and June quarters expected to flow into the September quarter.
Copper pass-through lag remains 3 to 6 months; management aims to reduce it to about one month or 15 days.
Capex for the current year is budgeted to be funded from internal accruals.
Management indicated new expansion plans may be announced in coming quarters once the 80% utilisation threshold is approached and customer forecasts firm up.
capex_capacity: Greenfield plants are ramping up; utilisation is at the same level as the prior quarter, with improvement noted and some plants still scaling.
Management said it expands capacity once overall utilisation reaches about 80%; it expects to announce new expansion in the next few quarters, but no specific new plant was named.
Current-year capex budget to be funded from internal accruals; no new debt planned for it.
Management said greenfield plants should merge into the regular business after a few months and deliver margins similar to existing plants, with the scalability gap attributed to productivity.
demand_pricing: Revenue grew 37% YoY, with ~7 pp from copper inflation and the remainder from volume growth, content increase, premiumisation and new OEM model launches.
Customer-specified components are priced through mutual negotiation with suppliers and customers; plastic and other input increases are not an automatic pass-through.
Management said the company has seen content per vehicle rise, not fall, under new architectures, and it is a design partner for future Japanese OEM vehicles.
Management is engine-agnostic, supplying leading ICE and EV platforms in India.

qa_highlights.question: How have greenfield plants performed in Q1 in revenue and EBITDA, and has break-even held?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even was achieved last quarter and maintained at ~INR450 crore run-rate. Profit contribution is expected in one or two quarters as plants ramp. Plant-level profitability is not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will wage hike impact be passed through, and by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said talks are constructive but no timeline can be given. It declined to quantify expected recovery, citing confidentiality, and said customers recognise the cost as manpower-linked.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR600 crore employee cost is attributable to minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase was largely from minimum wage hikes, with NCR wages up 30-40%, and the change QoQ is largely due to this. It did not give a specific number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the copper pass-through shortfall now?
qa_highlights.answer: The lag delta is about 7% in the current results, versus 17% in the prior quarter. Quarterly resets are done; 6-month-cycle customers are still pending. Most customers are on a 3-month basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin return to 34-35% in six months if raw material costs stay flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first priority is to recover costs to normalised levels. It added that after cost recovery, the sales-to-raw-material ratio will not match the past, and margin improvement is a medium-term goal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of new zonal or 48V architectures on content per vehicle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is ready to supply any architecture, has not seen de-contenting in India, and sees content rising with features. It acknowledged that long-term simplification is possible but said it would take a very long time.

risks_watch: Copper pass-through lag of 3 to 6 months; a 7% QoQ delta remains in Q1 results and will flow into Q2 as some price hikes are pending.
Minimum wage increases in other states remain unresolved, so the staff cost line may rise further.
Greenfield plants are not yet profit-accretive; watch whether they turn profitable in the next one or two quarters.
Management gave no quantified recovery of wage cost; customer negotiations are open-ended.
Long-term risk from zonal and 48V architectures simplifying harnesses, though management sees limited near-term impact.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and customer relationships, but cautious and evasive on cost recovery: management repeatedly declined to quantify wage pass-through, plant-level profitability and timelines. Management called the quarter a 'work in progress' in closing remarks.
